To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) it is possible to achieve a good load balance with a short-path length in a wireless network; (ii) it is possible, in a wireless network, to make routing decisions by local information and achieve a good load balanced routing; and (iii) the load-balanced routing algorithm is robust against dynamic topology changes.
we present a new class of wireless network algorithms that use only short routing paths, are load-balanced, and use local information for making routing decisions.

(i) the load-balance and the path length are two important and conflicting objectives for wireless routing, and (ii) we can achieve good performance in both of them simultaneously, by using only local information.

, in the context of wireless networks, it is possible to design algorithms that achieve good balance in both path lengths and load, even when the network topology is not known a priori.
